reviews.t: I lost literally everything. I have a terminally ill severely disabled 21 year old. I’m with him 24/7. I have no one. I also lost my job, my father died, I found his body… I worked for him my entire life. I literally lost everything, as did my boys and we have never been cared about. Always felt like a hassle for them, they’re rude, they pick and choose…very clicky people. We’ve had literally no one and they have not been a Blessing at all.

The Blessing Project is truly a lifeline for Swannanoa and the surrounding community. It is not just a nonprofit - it is a living example of what community care looks like in action. What they do goes far beyond providing food or basic resources. They offer hope, stability, and genuine human kindness to people who are going through some of the hardest moments of their lives. Their work supports families and individuals who would otherwise have nowhere to turn, and they do it with compassion, respect, and dignity. Kristen pours her heart and soul into this work. Her dedication and genuine love for this community are unmistakable. She doesn’t do this for recognition or praise but because she deeply cares about people and believes everyone deserves support and kindness. That spirit carries through the entire organization and every volunteer involved. The Blessing Project has changed lives and strengthened the fabric of our community in ways that can’t be overstated. Organizations like this are rare, and the good they’ve done speaks far louder than any misinformation ever could. They embody what it means to care for your community, and history will remember the way they showed up when it mattered the most.

I have volunteered at this organization/ministry, and these people are the real deal! Reaching out to help those who are in need of various things to survive or to better the lives of their children is what the ministry does. No judgement, no long documents to fill out. Just simply showing the love of Jesus with what God provides through donations and sacrifices made by those who want to help. Lives are being touched and souls are being fed through the leaders of this fine organization.

Kristen at the Blessing Barn has the kindest heart of anyone I've ever met. She gives constantly. Her job is unending as she tries to meet as many needs as possible in our community. She is a good steward of the donations she receives, constantly trying to determine the people who have actual needs and those who are just entitled and take more than their share. She gives with kindness and a pure heart but will not allow people to take advantage of the resources that are given to the Blessing Barn, because the resources are limited and are allocated for needs, not wants. If you read a bad review about Kristen or the Blessing Barn, that is from someone who is showing entitlement and selfishness. The purpose of this nonprofit is not to buy expensive items for people. It is to meet NEEDS.

These people have to be the biggest scam artists I’ve ever met! The audacity to scam people in need is so wild to me! My wife and I have a baby due and The Blessing Project told us that they would purchase the stroller and car seat for us and to choose the one we wanted! So we chose the one we wanted which was a 2 seater stroller and one car seat for roughly $280. Well the car seat and stroller they ordered for us came and it was only a one seater stroller and car seat (and they were pink) combo. We contacted them and they told us they made a mistake and would order the right one and to just send the incorrect one back! We told them it was not a big deal and that we would keep this one if they would not for sure order the correct one because we couldn’t be left with nothing at all! They swore to us they would order the right one and to just send the other one back and for us to not worry. So they ended up just stop responding to our texts or messages and then eventually told us that they refuse to order the right one and they are not going to be sending us the one we had back or let us pick one that was cheaper! ($280 for a 2 seat stroller and car seat combo is very cheap!) They still said no! They said they will not be giving us anything at all. It’s kind of sad that you could really help someone that’s in need and then strip them of it and take their help away altogether. Yall should be embarrassed and do not EVER claim to be a Christian organization because yall ARE NOT. You can’t promise something to people and give something to someone and take it back. That’s disgusting behavior especially from a “non profit” . And then on top of everything they were rude about it! By saying “We won’t be getting the one you asked for or anything else and honestly we’re surprised you asked.” I can’t wait to see what God has in store for people like this!

The Blessing Barn is such a nice option to have for folks in need. Everyone has always treated me with dignity and respect and I have always left with the supplies I needed. The owner is a wonderful person and her organization has done so much for this community.

This is a very inviting place for local neighbors to get help with food and other household supplies on Tuesday's and Thursday's from 10 a.m- 2p.m. Kristin and Charles are great and the other volunteers are helpful as well. One of my clients who has autism volunteers here. They also have hot meals delivered for the community in need. At the start of every day they are open, they pray with the volunteers amd community before opening the barn up to others for supplies. Kristin and Charles welcome all who want to be prayed for and to commit their lives to the Lord to come forward and they will pray with them.You can't find a more welcoming bunch who really care for our community. They will be moving locations next week so watch their Facebook website for new location and hours.

I’m so thankful for the Blessing Barn and all they’re doing for our community—especially during a time when so many are still in need of support. From the moment you walk in, you're greeted with a warm smile and the sweetest Southern hello! The "barn" is thoughtfully stocked with essentials, food, and even a special little corner just for kids to shop. Our family has been especially grateful for the propane exchanges they've provided when we needed it most. Thank you, Blessing Barn, for always showing up and giving so generously to the people of WNC. Your kindness truly makes a difference!

Most definitely one of my favorite places to visit in Buncombe county. Kristen and her entire crew of volunteers are some of the best, most kind hearted folks I've ever encountered. Iove to guys! Keep up the great work!!

I felt a calling to go to Asheville/Swananoa over Thanksgiving. I met Kristin on my journey and I was able to serve and donate. God places people in our lives and our hearts. This lady is so full of love and generosity. If you can give, please do so. If you are in need, go to Blessing Barn. Meet our little earthly angel. ❤️❤️
